question.worked_solution:
First, we use the power rule to simplify the right-hand side. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(x-2) & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{log}⁡(256) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(x-2) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({256}^{1/4}) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(x-2) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(x-2) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(4) \\ x-2 & =4 \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=6$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(x-2) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(6-2) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡(4) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡({256}^{1/4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{log}⁡(256).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=6$ is a valid solution.
